rules.message: A plain-`http://` URL STRING LITERAL in source. What is measured is the literal alone: nothing proves it is ever used as a request target (it may be an id, a docs link, or dead config), and nothing observes whether the page using it is served over https — so "mixed content" is the risk this names, not a fact it establishes. When the literal IS a request target from an https-served app, browsers block it as mixed content, or otherwise silently downgrade that request to no TLS. Use https, or route through an env-based/configurable base URL for internal service hosts — the private-IP/localhost exclude on this rule does not cover hostnames that resolve internally without a literal private IP, or https-required internal proxies.

A committed localhost/private-IP URL STRING LITERAL — the literal is what is measured; nothing proves it is used as a request target, only that it is hardcoded in source rather than read from env/config. When it is one, it breaks outside the dev machine. Move it to env/config; if this file is genuinely dev-only, add it to this rule's config `exclude` list (a path substring or glob) instead of disabling the rule everywhere.

A GET request carrying a body (a VALUE-position `method: 'get'` alongside `body:` in the same function) — servers/proxies may silently drop the body on a GET, so data the caller thinks it's sending never arrives. Use POST (or another body-bearing method) or move the data to query params. A TypeScript type-position `method: "GET" | "POST"` union (the common generic request-wrapper signature) is deliberately NOT matched — there the method is a parameter, not a committed GET, so the wrapper's conditional `body:` is fine. A file whose first 8 lines carry a machine-generated banner comment (`@generated`, `auto-generated`/`autogenerated`, `automatically generated`, `code generated by`, `this file is generated`, `this file was generated`, `openapi-generator`) is skipped WHOLE: the GET-with-body IS the generator's output, so switching it to POST or moving the data to query params is undone by the next regeneration. That banner list is COMPILED INTO this rule and does NOT read `vocabulary.generatedFileMarkers` — that config key reaches only the dead-code analyses (`unimported-export`, `dead-candidates`), so a house generator whose output carries a different banner — or no banner at all — is still flagged here, and the answer in either case is an `exclude` entry for its path.

WebSocket opened/upgraded (`new WebSocket(...)`/`.upgrade(...)`) with no auth material (`token`/`auth`/`session`/`cookie`/`jwt`) in the same function — an unauthenticated realtime channel lets anyone who can reach the socket connect. The WebSocket API can't set custom headers on the handshake, so instead use a short-lived one-time ticket/token in the WS URL's query string exchanged server-side, rely on same-origin cookies (sent automatically on the upgrade), or authenticate via the first message sent over the socket.
